Data project10.1M rows

EPA Air Quality

SQL analysis · 40 years of US air quality

Where, when and why does US air quality still cross the unhealthy AQI 100 line — and has it really improved since 1980?

Approach

Staged 10.1M daily county-level AQI records in PostgreSQL, ran data-quality checks, rebuilt them as a dimension and fact schema, then analysed trends, seasonality and dominant pollutants with CTEs and window functions.

Key findings

  • Unhealthy county-days fell from 18.9% in 1980 to 1.5% in 2020, and the decline holds after controlling for monitor coverage — but it has been flat since 2013.
  • Nine counties (eight in California, plus Maricopa, AZ) exceeded 5% unhealthy days in every year since 1980.
  • Ozone drives 80.2% of unhealthy summer days nationally, while sulfur dioxide drives 99.4% in Hawaii.

So what: Prioritise summer ozone control in Southern California and the Central Valley, and plan a separate SO2 alert approach for Hawaii.

Built with

  • PostgreSQL
  • SQL
  • CTEs
  • Window functions
  • Data cleaning

Data project119K bookings

Hotel Booking Demand

Power BI dashboard · Cancellation & demand

Which kinds of hotel bookings are most likely to be cancelled, and which policies are worth testing to reduce it?

Approach

Cleaned 119,390 raw booking records down to 119,208 with Python (pandas), modelled them in Power BI with DAX measures and a calendar table, and built a three-page dashboard covering cancellation, seasonal demand and City versus Resort.

Key findings

  • Cancellation climbs with lead time: 9.6% for bookings made 0–7 days ahead, 55.5% at 181–365 days and 67.7% beyond a year.
  • City Hotel cancels more than Resort Hotel (41.8% vs 27.8%), driven by higher cancellation at long lead times rather than more long-lead bookings.
  • Travel agent and tour operator channels hold 82% of bookings at 41.1% cancellation, against 17.5% for Direct.

So what: Hypotheses worth piloting: stricter deposit or cancellation windows for long-lead City Hotel bookings, and incentives for direct booking.

Built with

Data project5.8M flights

Flight Delays

SQL analysis · US domestic flights, 2015

Which US airlines are the most reliable, when and where do delays peak, and what actually causes them?

Approach

Loaded 5.8M flight records into PostgreSQL, validated the joins across three tables (which exposed unmapped airport codes for October), then analysed airlines, months, airports and delay causes with CTEs, window functions and rankings.

Key findings

  • Alaska, Delta and Hawaiian beat the national average on both delays and cancellations; 29.7% of Spirit and 26.2% of Frontier flights arrived 15+ minutes late (national: 18.6%).
  • Late-arriving aircraft cause 39.8% of delay minutes; extreme weather causes only 5.0% of delay minutes but 54.4% of cancellations.
  • June (23.5% late) and February (23.4%) are the worst months; September and October are the smoothest.

So what: Pick carriers and months with the lowest risk, and leave extra buffer for tight same-day connections.

Built with

Data project150K sample

US Used Cars

Price analysis & prediction · Python

What drives the resale value of used cars in the US, and how accurately can price be predicted?

Approach

Sampled 10% of 1.5M used-car listings in chunks, cleaned them to 149,715 rows, explored depreciation and brand value retention, then compared Linear Regression with XGBoost on log price, using permutation importance to rank features.

Key findings

  • Prices drop 25.9% in the first year; after age 8, cars lose about $1,000 a year or less.
  • Toyota and Hyundai keep 64.4% of their value between ages 0–2 and 5–7, versus 44.2% for Chrysler and 44.8% for BMW.
  • XGBoost predicts price with MAE $1,901 and R² 0.941, against MAE $3,426 and R² 0.804 for the Linear Regression baseline.

So what: Dealers should favour high-retention brands and body types; buyers get the best value at age 4–5 or 8–11.
